resolutions.researcher_notes: UBTG = Uthmaniyah-Berri Trunk Gas, part of Aramco's Master Gas System (MGS). Aramco's own MGS article (via Wayback; aramco.com times out the verifier) describes the MGS as a long-operating pipeline network (on stream since 1982, Berri/Uthmaniyah plants). Saudipedia (independent) corroborates the MGS/Hawiyah gas infrastructure as operational and Aramco-run. Both support 'operating' at the parent-system level; neither names this specific GIS-auto-split km0-km56 segment (P1897-P1925 are Aramco internal route-database segments with no press footprint), hence medium not high.

Both sources establish the UBTG/MGS as a natural-gas transmission system (Master Gas System), supporting Fuel=Gas. (Note: on GEM gas rows the FuelSource field is the upstream field/plant, not 'Natural Gas'; here the unit value 'Gas' is the commodity, which the MGS designation supports.) Class-level support, not segment-specific.

LengthKnown=56.00 km is a GIS route-database segment length (km0 to km56 of the UBTG-1 trunk), machine-derived by GEM. No independent public source reports the length of this specific auto-split segment. UNRESOLVED as expected for the P1897-P1925 GIS-node-coded MGS segments.

Diameter=48 in is a segment-specific attribute from Aramco's internal route database. No independent public source confirms a 48-in diameter for this exact km0-km56 segment (the parent UBTG-1 trunk rows carry mixed 56/36/38/40/42-in in GEM). UNRESOLVED; no source to corroborate the specific number.

The MGS and its Berri/Uthmaniyah/Hawiyah nodes are entirely within Saudi Arabia (Eastern Province, Ghawar/Al-Ahsa area), supporting StartCountryOrArea=EndCountryOrArea=Saudi Arabia. Only the country-level location is asserted in the unit values; both sources support it. Specific endpoints are the GIS node codes km0/km56, not independently sourceable.

Aramco's own MGS article establishes the Master Gas System (which the UBTG-1 Uthmaniyah-Berri trunk is part of) as Aramco-developed and Aramco-operated infrastructure; Saudipedia independently attributes the Hawiyah/MGS gas facilities to Saudi Aramco. Supports Owner1=Saudi Aramco 100%. No JV/subsidiary indicated for this trunk.
